Discord

DIS-kord — 'dis-' means apart, and the root relates to 'heart'; discord is hearts pulling apart, not together. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Discord is a lack of harmony between people or things; disagreement.

Constant discord between the two business partners eventually forced them to dissolve the company.

Worked Example

Two siblings who once shared everything begin arguing over every small decision after inheriting their parents' house together, until they can no longer sit in the same room without a fight breaking out.

That breakdown of harmony, where agreement turns into constant friction, is exactly what discord means. Unlike 'disagreement,' which can be a single moment, discord describes an ongoing state of conflict.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

disharmony: Disharmony is the flat absence of agreement or peace -- the parts simply fail to fit together, whether people, colors, or sounds. Discord is more active and human: an ongoing state of clashing, people repeatedly grinding against one another.

dissent: Dissent is open disagreement with a decision or an authority -- one voice saying no to a ruling. Discord needs no ruling and no rebel: it is the ongoing lack of harmony itself, a group that cannot stop clashing.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

harmony: agreement or peaceful cooperation

accord: agreement or a state of harmony

Where it sits · how deep the conflict runs — friction → discord → strife

friction vs. discord: Friction is milder than discord -- friction can be small, occasional tension, while discord describes a deeper, more lasting lack of harmony.

strife vs. discord: Strife can feel more intense than discord: discord is disagreement, but strife often implies real struggle or even hostility on top of that disagreement.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — dis-

prefix — dis-: apart, not (Latin)

root — -cord-

root — -cord-: heart (Latin (cor, cordis))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin cor/cordis meant 'heart.' Discord, at its root, means hearts pulled apart -- the opposite of being of one heart or mind.

Use the root in a new word: cordial

Use the root in a new word: cordial: The two leaders exchanged a cordial handshake despite their political differences.
